raw_response:
I'm seventy this year, and I've been farming these 7.7 mu in Quzhou for forty years. I studied at the agricultural college when I was young, so I understand nutrient budgets and the critical growth stages, but theory doesn't pump water or buy fertilizer. With only 7.7 mu and five people in the house—my wife, my son's family, and me—every yuan has to be justified. I split the land: 5 mu in wheat-maize double cropping, which is my grain base, and 2.7 mu in cotton for cash and risk diversification.

The wheat went in last October, Jimai 22 at 15 kg/mu. I applied base fertilizer then—about 12 kg N/mu as compound, plus phosphorus and a little potassium. Now it's late April, the wheat is at jointing, and I'm deciding on the topdress. The book says I could go to 25 kg N/mu for a 550 kg yield, but my neighbor Lao Zhang tried that last year and only got thirty kilos more than me while spending a lot extra on urea. I'm targeting 480 kg/mu, and with urea at 2.6 yuan per kilo this spring, I'll topdress 8 kg N/mu now, bringing the total to 20 kg N/mu. That's my compromise. I'll irrigate three times: now at jointing, once at heading, and once at grain filling. Each irrigation costs nearly 40 yuan/mu in electricity, so three is my hard limit.

Come early June, I have maybe five days between wheat harvest and maize planting. I'll plant Zhengdan 958, a hybrid, at 2.5 kg/mu. I'll put down base fertilizer with the planter—about 12 kg N/mu and some P—and topdress another 6 kg N at the big flare stage. Two irrigations: one at jointing, one at silking. If the summer turns dry, I might regret not budgeting for a third, but the well meter doesn't forgive, and I'd rather have cash in hand for emergencies.

The cotton goes in now on the 2.7 mu plot. I'll use an improved variety, about 1.5 kg seed per mu. Base fertilizer before planting: roughly 10 kg N, 4 kg P, 6 kg K per mu, then another 4 kg N at early flowering. Cotton is labor-intensive—my daughter-in-law will help with picking in autumn—but it gives me cash when grain prices are low. I'll irrigate twice and spray for bollworm three to four times. I'm expecting about 280 kg/mu of seed cotton.

Total input cost this year will be around 4,500 yuan. That's a heavy load on a 7.7-mu farm, but cutting back on phosphorus or skipping an irrigation would cost me more in lost yield than I'd save. Still, I'm mixing my own fertilizer program from urea and diammonium phosphate rather than buying expensive compound blends—saves about fifteen percent. At my age, I'm not chasing maximum yield; I'm chasing stability and making sure I don't lose money.
